pageStatus: skeleton default: real inference via local MoveNet MultiPose with SinglePose Thunder mode; action default: real inference via local pose-sequence classifier; mechanism: preset teaching demo

decision.reason: MoveNet returns COCO-style 17 keypoints directly in the browser and fits the teaching page. MultiPose Lightning is used as the skeleton page default because it can detect up to 6 people; SinglePose Thunder remains available as the higher-accuracy single-person mode and Lightning remains a local fallback. A full pretrained C3D/MoViNet browser video classifier remains heavy, so this round connects a lightweight local pose-sequence classifier that performs real model forward inference over the action frame sequence.

connectedModels.label: TensorFlow.js MoveNet MultiPose Lightning
connectedModels.runtime: TensorFlow.js CPU backend by default; WebGL backend script kept available for acceleration
connectedModels.outputSchema: Up to 6 COCO-style poses; each pose has keypoints with x, y and score plus a bounding box
connectedModels.fallback: If MultiPose detector creation fails, the page automatically tries local SinglePose Thunder and then local SinglePose Lightning before falling back to preset COCO-17 samples.

connectedModels.label: TensorFlow.js MoveNet SinglePose Thunder
connectedModels.runtime: TensorFlow.js CPU backend by default; WebGL backend script kept available for acceleration
connectedModels.outputSchema: COCO-style keypoints with x, y and score
connectedModels.fallback: Used by the single-person high-accuracy mode. If Thunder detector creation fails, the page automatically tries local MoveNet Lightning before falling back to preset COCO-17 samples.

connectedModels.label: TensorFlow.js MoveNet SinglePose Lightning
connectedModels.runtime: TensorFlow.js CPU backend by default; WebGL backend script kept available for acceleration
connectedModels.outputSchema: COCO-style keypoints with x, y and score
connectedModels.fallback: Used only if local Thunder detector creation fails. If runtime or both local models fail, the page keeps the preset COCO-17 sample and labels the state as preset fallback.

connectedModels.label: Local Pose Sequence Action Classifier
connectedModels.runtime: Vanilla JavaScript linear softmax over pose-sequence features
connectedModels.inputSchema: 14 pose-sequence motion features from generated frame keypoints
connectedModels.fallback: If the local classifier JSON fails to load, the action page keeps JSON fallback probabilities and labels the state as preset fallback.
connectedModels.note: This is a lightweight local classroom classifier, not a pretrained C3D/MoViNet video model.

candidateModels.label: MediaPipe Pose Landmarker Web
candidateModels.assessment: Good browser pose option, but it uses a 33-landmark schema and a MediaPipe task bundle. MoveNet was a closer fit for the current COCO-17 teaching page.

candidateModels.label: ONNX Runtime Web
candidateModels.assessment: The browser runtime is suitable, but a small, ready, COCO-17 ONNX pose model with simple browser preprocessing/postprocessing was not selected in this round.

candidateModels.label: MoViNet streaming action recognition
candidateModels.assessment: Good reference for action recognition, but not directly wired into this Flask/Jinja browser page in this round. The action page now uses a local pose-sequence classifier for real probability inference while keeping the C3D/3D Conv view as a mechanism visualization.
